subject: Renewal pricing — multi-year rate safeguard proposal
messages:
From: Carly Patel <carly.patel@bluestoneanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@bluestoneanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — need price protection and predictable ramp

Connor —

Thanks for the draft renewal note. Our finance team is concerned about potential rate inflation next year; before we commit we need a clear multi-year option that: 1) locks unit price for at least 24 months, 2) allows a staged ramp on committed capacity, and 3) includes a fair true-up mechanism (we prefer credits rather than surprise invoices).

High-level requirements:
- Start-of-contract committed QPS/TPU equivalent: 1.0M tokens/mo (year 1) ramping to 2.0M tokens/mo by month 9.
- Prefer a 2-year agreement with renewal pricing fixed for the term.
- We may need an escape for material downtimes > 6 hours per month.

Can you outline what discounts you can offer under a 2-year prepay (annual vs. multi-year invoice), how breakage/true-up works, and the invoicing cadence?

Also, please include an example amortization schedule we can share with procurement.

Regards,
Carly
Carly Patel
Head of Data Platform
BlueStone Analytics

(Attachment: bluestone_current_usage_q3.csv)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Carly Patel <carly.patel@bluestoneanalytics.com>
Cc: Rajesh Menon <rajesh.m@bluestoneanalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — need price protection and predictable ramp

Hi Carly —

Appreciate the clear requirements — totally doable and thanks for sending the usage file. At a high level we can offer two structured options for a 24-month commitment:

Option A — Multi-year prepaid (single invoice):
- 15% off list unit price for the first 12 months, 12% off for months 13–24 (blended effective ~13.5%).
- Prepaid invoice at contract start covering full 24 months.
- Staged ramp: you can start at 50% of committed tokens for months 1–3, then 75% months 4–6, full capacity month 7 onward with true-up credit for under-utilization applied at 12- and 24-month checkpoints.
- Breakage credit: unconsumed prepaid funds convert to usage credit for 12 months after expiry; after that remaining value is forfeited.

Option B — Annual prepay (two invoices):
- 14% off Y1, 13% off Y2; each year prepaid separately with a 30-day invoice window.
- Allows you to decouple years if you want flexibility, but price protection only for the paid year.

We can also add a limited price-parachute clause: if we change published list prices upward during the term, your effective committed unit price will be capped to the higher of the contracted rate or a 3% annual cap.

I'll put together a term sheet and an amortization example (monthly/quarterly) and get legal/finance eyes on the breakage language. Are you leaning toward single prepaid vs. annual invoicing? If you prefer, we can do a hybrid (50% prepaid at start, remainder invoiced annually at an additional 10% discount).

Thanks —
Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Carly Patel <carly.patel@bluestoneanalytics.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — need price protection and predictable ramp

Connor —

Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifying questions from procurement/finance:
- For Option A, if we prepays and then underutilize in year 1, you say credits are applied at 12mo — will that be a cash refund or account credit? Procurement prefers credits with a 24mo window.
- Can you shorten the staged ramp to fully ramp by month 6? Our onboarding can accelerate.
- What happens if our usage overshoots the committed level in year 2 — do we pay list for overages or an overage rate?
- Will you accept a PO + net-30 for the prepaid invoice (finance prefers to start with PO evidence even if we net-30 the remaining settlement).

Also, given we are an enterprise customer with regulatory constraints, we need the SLO language tied to credits for downtime > the stated thresholds.

If you can send a redlined term sheet addressing these, I can get procurement to review next week.

Best,
Carly

Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion — BlueStone — ask on multi-year prepay structure

Marissa / Sean —

Forwarding inbound from BlueStone (Carly). Key asks: 24-month price lock, staged ramp (they want faster ramp, up to month 6), credits for underutilization with 24mo window, and PO + net-30 for a prepaid invoice.

Proposed offer to push back as a firm commercial that balances revenue and customer needs:
- 24-month prepaid (single invoice) with 14.5% blended discount (15% Y1 / 12% Y2).
- Ramp: 50% months 1–2, 75% months 3–5, 100% month 6 onward (accelerated per their ask).
- Underutilization: account credit applied at 12mo and final 24mo checkpoint; credits valid 24 months from issuance. No cash refunds.
- Overages: billed at contracted committed rate + 25% premium (capped at list price).
- Invoicing: we will accept a PO reference and invoice net-30; full prepay due within 30 days of invoice.
- SLA: credit-based SLOs; legal to propose specifics.

Questions: acceptable to trade a slightly lower Y2 discount (12%) for a stronger price lock and 24mo credit window? Also need finance/legal to confirm breakage accounting and recognition.

Attaching a draft term sheet and the amortization example for quick review. Please advise if you want to propose Option B instead.

Thanks —
Connor

Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion — BlueStone — ask on multi-year prepay structure

Connor / Sean —

This is a reasonable commercial to take to the customer. I have two suggested tweaks to improve win probability and keep revenue protected:
1) Make the Y1 discount 16% and Y2 12% (blended ~14%); we can absorb a bit more upfront to lock the logo for two years.
2) Add a breakage reallocation: if credits remain unused after the 24-month window, 50% of remaining credit can be applied to any other Redwood product purchases at BlueStone within 12 months (shows flexibility and limits accounting churn).

Legal/Finance need to confirm recognition for our ARR, but I think procurement will like the 24mo credit window and PO + net-30. On the SLA side, include a monthly uptime target and a capped credit per month equal to 5% of that month's committed value.

If those tweaks are OK, let's send a clean term sheet for signature and propose a DocuSign route for speed.

-Marissa

- Structure: 24-month prepaid (single invoice) with PO accepted as reference and payment due net-30.
- Pricing: 16% off list for Year 1, 12% off list for Year 2. Blended discount ~14%.
- Ramp: 50% months 1–2, 75% months 3–5, 100% month 6 onward.

- Price protection: effective committed unit price capped by a 3% annual list price uplift (price-parachute).
- SLA: monthly uptime target tied to credit-based remediation; maximum monthly credit = 5% of that month's committed value.
